_comment: The hand-maintained half of the status tracker. Everything a file in the repo already
knows -- commit list, diffstat, baseline rows, counter count -- is derived by
build-status.py and must NOT be typed here.
What belongs here: a one-line verdict per work item, its status, the commits it spans,
and a pointer to the doc section that owns the reasoning. Do not restate the reasoning.
docs/porting/00-master-plan.md is the source of truth; a second copy of an argument is a
second thing to keep in sync, and this repo has already paid for that once (938a472).
status: landed | refuted | cancelled | reverted | open | deferred | blocked
refuted   hypothesis tested against a control and found false
cancelled killed by its own gate before being built
reverted  built, measured, removed -- only the finding kept
area:   platform | cpu | graphics | audio | input | tooling | docs
Adding work: append an item naming its commits, then run build-status.py. Any fork
commit no item claims is rendered on the page as unattributed, so nothing goes missing.
title: TesseraEmu — fork status
tagline: A hard fork of Cemu retargeted at Apple Silicon and macOS 26 only: one architecture, one renderer, and a measured record of everything tried — including the two thirds of it that did not work.
summary: arm64 only, macOS 26.0 minimum, Metal only. Upstream Cemu is portable; this fork deliberately is not. `precompiled.h` refuses to compile on any other target, `BackendX64/` and the IML x86 machinery are gone, and the binary links Metal and QuartzCore and nothing else graphical.

headline.label: Mario Kart 8, locked
headline.note: at ~104% of one core, down from ~184% before the idle-spin work

headline.label: BotW open world (Korok Forest)
headline.note: **30.06** with `GX2DrawdoneSync` off — a config default, not the renderer

headline.label: of active GPU samples are ALU-limited
headline.note: texture sampling 22.8%; the whole memory path only 12.8%

headline.label: refuted attempts at the same 1.90 ms
headline.note: ordering- and bandwidth-shaped work is now closed by measurement

divergence.title: Deleted outright
entries: The **OpenGL and Vulkan/MoltenVK backends**, the GLSL shader emitter and glslang. Metal is the only renderer.
The **x86-64 recompiler backend** and all x86 IML machinery, including the only backend peephole pass that existed.
x86 SIMD paths in `cpu_features`, Carbon key codes, the self-updater, and the portability shims that assumed a second architecture or backend.
`#ifdef ARCH_X86_64` and runtime arch/backend checks. If something looks like it needs one, it does not.

divergence.title: Rewritten for this hardware
entries: `cpu_features` for arm64; title and content decryption onto the **ARMv8 AES extensions**, validated against FIPS-197 by a standalone probe.
`FSpinlock` is now `os_unfair_lock` — a raw spin on an asymmetric-core CPU can burn a P-core against a descheduled E-core holder.

**Thread QoS with a P/E split.** Guest cores and the GPU command thread `USER_INTERACTIVE`; compile pools sized against the efficiency cluster instead of `hardware_concurrency()`, which was spawning 17 threads on a 4P+4E machine.
Audio onto a **lock-free SPSC ring** — the mixer had been taking a mutex on CoreAudio's realtime thread.
`MemMapper` for **16 KB pages**, screensaver inhibition through `NSProcessInfo`, and SDL input off a 5 ms main-thread timer.

divergence.title: Added
entries: A **telemetry harness compiled into the core** — counters across GPU, CPU, memory and accuracy, `__thread`-local and cache-line striped, gated on one branch so a disabled build measurably costs nothing.
A **golden-scene capture harness** (`testing/capture-scene.sh`) and a scripted BotW driver that reaches a repeatable scene with no human and no save file.
A **code-anchored Wii U hardware reference** — ten documents in `docs/hardware/`, written against the emulator's own source rather than wiki lore. Writing it found two bugs.

A native **GameController.framework** input provider, crash diagnostics (`sigaltstack`, arm64 PC recovery, demangled backtraces), CMake-driven bundle signing, and standalone probes in `tools/probes/`.

divergence.title: Bugs the port surfaced
entries: **248 bytes of heap corruption on every startup** — the Metal renderer initialised a `[3][31]` array with a loop bound of 4. It was the real cause of a long-standing `// HACK: ... garbage data` workaround.

`MemMapper` rounded a mapping's base but not its length and did no rounding at all on unmap, so releasing a guest range failed silently and left it writable across a title switch. 16 KB pages make this reachable where 4 KB pages hid it.
The AArch64 backend left the emitter cursor short of the end of generated code, so `readyRE()` **invalidated only part of the I-cache** — a stale-instruction hazard on cold paths only.

Graphic packs corrupting GPU registers; sampler LOD bias never applied at all; an `MTLEvent` value wrap that silently disabled command-buffer serialisation every ~29 s; a missing `NSHighResolutionCapable` handing Metal a half-resolution drawable.

tables.title: The two BotW scenes, and why the open world is the interesting one
tables.note: `testing/drive-botw.sh` reaches the Shrine of Resurrection unattended. A Korok Forest save is the heavier scene and the one every current graphics conclusion rests on. **The Shrine column is not current** — it predates the `839466d` `busy_ns` fix and two different instruments disagree about it; re-measure before quoting it.

tables.title: The 49.90 ms Korok frame, fully decomposed
tables.note: Nothing is saturated. Guest cores ~18% busy, GPU ~33% busy, command processor ~71% waiting. The frame is three whole vsync slots because `gpu.frame_critical_path_ns` is 35.25 ms against a two-slot deadline of 33.27 ms — it misses by **1.90 ms** and drops to the next division rather than degrading smoothly.
rows: Latte thread waiting for guest commands (`cp_idle`)

tables.title: What actually limits the GPU — and it is not bandwidth
tables.note: `Metal GPU Counters`, Korok gameplay, 179,221 samples, conditioned on the 42.1% where some limiter exceeds 5%. **ALU and texture are the bottleneck in 86.1% of active samples; the memory path in 12.8%.** `Partial Renders Count` is 0 everywhere — no tile-memory spills. This is the measurement that cancelled the streamout work.
columns: share where it is THE top limiter

tables.title: The accuracy-for-speed levers — measured, neither default changed
tables.note: Two settings trade correctness for frame rate. Recording what each costs so the leave-it-on decision is informed rather than inherited. Changing a default is a product call, not an engineering one.
rows: **20.04 → 30.06 fps** on Korok; critical path 35.25 → 18.64 ms; intra-frame GPU gap 16.39 → 0.25 ms (n=3 / n=2)
The guest asks for a full pipeline drain and does not get one. BotW reads back 21 KB of GPU-computed floats per frame that it genuinely consumes.
unavailable; the fork already runs as if it were off, so its speed is banked in every number here
Already being paid: anything sampling a render target while writing it reads undefined data. BotW lava and waterfalls are the known cases.

items.title: Stage 1 — a Metal-first baseline that boots on arm64
items.verdict: First running arm64 build with Metal as the only configured renderer. Carried the fix for the `[3][31]`-array constructor overflow and moved decryption onto the ARMv8 AES extensions.
items.note: The overflow had been papered over by a `// HACK: ... garbage data` comment for years. Root-causing it deleted both the hack and the bug.

items.title: Delete the OpenGL and Vulkan backends
items.verdict: Metal is the only renderer. The GLSL emitter and glslang went with them.
items.note: Deleting a backend exposes coupling only the linker finds: the MSL emitter forward-declared four helpers that were **defined in the GLSL emitter's translation unit**, and several files were receiving `robin_hood` and `StringBuf` only transitively through Vulkan includes.

items.title: The documented one-`MAP_JIT`-region-per-process limit is not enforced
items.verdict: 4,000 regions succeed under hardened runtime on macOS 26. The risk this would have forced a custom JIT allocator is retired.
items.note: A first probe appeared to confirm the limit — it was testing an RWX pattern xbyak never uses. **Probe the pattern the code actually uses, not the one the docs describe.** Preserved in `tools/probes/`.

items.title: Remove the stale macOS "preview version" disclaimer
items.verdict: Upstream's warning that macOS is a preview is not true of a fork that targets only macOS. Also started ignoring `Roms/`.

items.title: Golden-scene capture harness
items.verdict: `testing/capture-scene.sh` records a window-only frame plus FPS/RSS/threads into `testing/golden/baseline.tsv`, which is the committed record every claim here is checked against.
items.note: There is no test suite in this repo. Verification is: it builds, it boots a title, the frame looks right, and nothing new appears in the log. The harness is what makes the last two checkable.

items.title: Delete the x86-64 recompiler backend and all x86 IML machinery
items.verdict: `BackendX64/` is gone. The `IMLUtil_*` helpers were kept as substrate for an AArch64 replacement.
items.note: The only backend peephole pass that existed was x86-specific and went with it — there is currently **no backend peephole pass at all**.

items.title: Rewrite `cpu_features` for arm64
items.verdict: The remaining x86 SIMD paths are gone. `g_CPUFeatures` now exposes `performanceCores` / `efficiencyCores`, which is what lets worker pools be sized against the right cluster.

items.title: Target macOS 26 / arm64 only; normalize the architecture macros
items.verdict: `precompiled.h` `#error`s on any other target. CMake hygiene alongside it: the inactive AppleClang warning fixed, and LTO left off in `RelWithDebInfo` deliberately.
items.note: LTO off keeps relinks fast and keeps `.o` files real Mach-O so `llvm-objdump` can inspect generated code. `Release` turns ThinLTO on and the objects become LLVM bitcode.

items.title: Fix 16 KB page handling in `MemMapper` and the MMU range table
items.verdict: Mapping rounded the base but not the length, and unmapping rounded nothing — so releasing a guest range failed silently with `EINVAL` and left it writable across a title switch.
items.note: Apple Silicon's 16 KB pages make this reachable where 4 KB pages hid it. A real bug the port surfaced rather than introduced.

items.title: Fix the JIT code-size and emitter-cursor bugs in the AArch64 backend
items.verdict: The cursor stopped short of the end of generated code, so `readyRE()` invalidated only part of the I-cache — a stale-instruction hazard that surfaces only on cold paths.
items.note: The follow-up corrected a docs claim that xbyak performs no I-cache maintenance. It does.

items.title: Sign the app bundle from CMake; split release and debug entitlements
items.verdict: Signing happens inner-out — nested dylibs first, bundle last — as part of the build rather than as a manual step.

items.title: Crash diagnostics: alternate signal stack, arm64 PC recovery, real backtraces
items.verdict: A stack-overflow SIGSEGV can now be reported instead of killing the handler, and backtraces are demangled with a recovered arm64 PC.

items.title: Instrument the JIT code leak instead of building reclamation for it
items.verdict: Epoch-based reclamation is a large piece of machinery for a leak nobody had measured. A counter went in first; reclamation waits on that counter showing a problem.

items.title: Stage 4 — `FSpinlock` becomes `os_unfair_lock`, then thread QoS
items.verdict: `SetThreadName(name, ThreadRole)` maps a role to a QoS class: guest cores and the GPU command thread `USER_INTERACTIVE`, compile and background work `UTILITY`. 16 call sites pass a role.
items.note: Order mattered. A raw spinlock plus QoS on asymmetric cores can hang; `os_unfair_lock` donates priority, so the lock change had to land first. `UTILITY` rather than `BACKGROUND` because macOS throttles the latter hard.

items.title: Audio: lock-free SPSC ring, and a latency request above the device floor
items.verdict: The mixer had been taking a mutex on CoreAudio's realtime thread — an unfixable priority inversion and a glitch source.
items.note: The fix is not QoS. Raising the audio thread's priority would have made the inversion worse, not better; the callback itself had to stop blocking.

items.title: Native macOS integration: screensaver, SDL event thread, Info.plist, no Carbon
items.verdict: Screensaver inhibition through `NSProcessInfo`; SDL input off a 5 ms main-thread timer onto its own thread; Carbon key codes dropped; `NSHighResolutionCapable` added.
items.note: Without `NSHighResolutionCapable` macOS ran the whole app magnified and handed Metal a **half-resolution drawable**. SDL's own screensaver path was disabled on macOS because it initialises `SDL_INIT_VIDEO` inside a wx app that already owns `NSApplication`.

items.title: Native `GameController.framework` input provider
items.verdict: A first-party input path that does not go through SDL.
items.note: `controllerProfiles/` ships empty, which is why input looks broken out of the box. Scripted driving writes a keyboard profile directly — the GUI combo boxes do not respond to accessibility scripting.

items.title: Three idle spins removed from the scheduler and command processor
items.verdict: **1.77× less total process CPU on Mario Kart 8 — 184% → 104% of one core — at an identical locked 60 FPS.**
items.note: An earlier baseline blamed `mach_continuous_time` at 47% self on the graphics idle path. Wrong caller: it was `__OSThreadCoreIdle` → `__OSCheckSystemEvents`, an unbounded busy-wait in the **scheduler**. Both idle-wait bugs were invisible to the `hostInstrCount / ppcInstrCount` metric the plan had ranked first — profile before picking a codegen target.

items.title: Apply sampler LOD bias, and stop graphic packs corrupting GPU registers
items.verdict: LOD bias was being computed and never applied. `MTLSamplerDescriptor.lodBias` is new in macOS 26.0, which a fork pinned to macOS 26 can simply use.

items.title: The TBDR work was rejected — then the rejection was found to be scene-dependent
items.verdict: The audit closed the whole TBDR workstream on the argument that the GPU was idle at 2.83 ms/frame. It had sampled the **MK8 title card**, not gameplay. On a real scene the GPU is at 87.7% of a 16.67 ms budget.
items.note: MK8's attract mode spends most of its wall-clock on the title card, so a short trace silently measures a near-idle scene. Gate on `draws/f > 200` to isolate race frames. The corrected verdict restored the graphics workstream and set the precondition — a GPU-heavy scene — under which the audit would later be redone.

items.title: Memoryless depth and load/store action audit
items.verdict: The safe wins are small and the large one needs pass-count work first. Later closed permanently for this scene: depth is **sampled by a shader on 390 draws/frame**, so `StoreActionDontCare` is not available.

items.title: The deferred texture copy is retired — the pass churn was buffer uploads
items.verdict: Built against the hypothesis that texture copies were breaking render passes. They were not; buffer uploads were. The mechanism was removed and the finding kept.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The render-pass churn was buffer uploads

items.title: A code-anchored Wii U hardware reference — and two bugs it found
items.verdict: Ten documents in `docs/hardware/`, written against the emulator's own source rather than wiki lore. Writing them surfaced two real bugs.

items.title: The telemetry harness — counters compiled into the core
items.verdict: X-macro `.def` → enum → `__thread` TLS rows, cache-line striped and summed at the frame boundary. Proven free when disabled *before* anything was instrumented. Every performance claim on this page comes from it.
items.note: Phase 1 deliberately re-derived a result already known by other means, as a check on the instrument. Phase 3 found BotW was missing 31 imports. The follow-up fixed a race and a hot-path allocation the harness itself had introduced.

items.title: Decompose the frame: the open world is not GPU-bound, it is vsync-quantised
items.verdict: Korok Forest issues **fewer** draws than the shrine and leaves the GPU idle 62% of the time, yet runs slower. 49.90 ms is exactly three vsync slots, and p99 equals the median — no variance, which is the signature of quantisation, not of variable work.

items.title: CPU counters: nothing is saturated
items.verdict: All three guest cores together are busy 26.89 ms of a 49.90 ms frame — **18% of three-core capacity**. There is no CPU wall to knock down.

items.title: 52,330 free HLE calls per frame, and where the context switches come from
items.verdict: Every HLE call advances guest time by **zero cycles**, including `FSReadFile`, which on hardware is an IPC round trip to IOSU. And **79.4% of the 3,143 thread switches per frame are the guest voluntarily calling `OSYieldThread`** — BotW polling, faithfully emulated, because Cafe OS scheduling is cooperative.
items.note: A flat per-call charge is ruled out by measurement, not opinion: `cpu.hle_would_charge_cycles` sums a hypothetical 500/call to **163% of the cycles actually retired**. The volume is `OSFastMutex_Lock/Unlock`, `OSGetCoreId` and GX2 register setters — tens of cycles each on hardware. Any charge must be tiered per function.

items.title: Park the GPU fence wait instead of spinning
items.verdict: One guest fence was being spun on **65 million times a second**. Parking it cut a further **20% of process CPU** in BotW with no frame-rate change.
items.note: No frame-rate change was the correct outcome and is now understood: the guest was never waiting for the GPU. See `cp-fence-vsync`.

items.title: Rebrand to TesseraEmu, and migrate the user data directory in place
items.verdict: Existing installs migrate rather than losing their saves and settings. Verified from the new path that nothing depended on the old one.

items.title: CI on the fork, and the bugs it was hiding
items.verdict: Getting the build check green turned out to require fixing two real bugs it had been failing to report.

items.title: Recover the translation sources, and an Arabic catalog broken twice over
items.verdict: The `.pot` generation check was added, then immediately broke the Arabic plural forms; both the check and the catalog were fixed.
items.note: ~30 changed `_()` strings across 19 locales are still untranslated — see the roadmap.

items.title: The README, rewritten around the fork and then corrected three times
items.verdict: Describes what this fork is rather than upstream Cemu. Two of the corrections were of numbers invalidated by the immediately preceding commits.
items.note: This is precisely the failure mode this status page exists to remove: hand-typed numbers going stale within two commits.

items.title: Measure the fiber switch: 454 ns, a 70× gap, and not a frame-rate fix
items.verdict: `swapcontext` costs **454.5 ns** against **6.5 ns** for a hand-written AArch64 switch — `swapcontext` on Darwin/arm64 calls `sigprocmask` on both save and restore. At 3,143 switches/frame that is **1.43 ms/frame**, 2.9% of the frame.
items.note: Worth doing for power and headroom, not for fps: the frame already fits its work into one vsync period with 16.6% headroom, so removing 1.4 ms crosses no boundary. A microbenchmark is the right instrument — `Fiber::Switch` does not return until the fiber is resumed, so an in-process scope timer measures descheduled time and reported 197 ms of "busy" inside a 49.9 ms frame.

items.title: Instrument three open questions at once; two answers killed the work
items.verdict: `IT_MEM_SEMAPHORE` and the wait-for-flip spin are **exactly zero** in BotW. Snapshotting guest threads at fence-stall entry found the cores idle 95% of the time — against a 96% baseline, so it discriminated nothing.
items.note: A probe with no control sample cannot discriminate. The 95%-vs-96% result is the cleanest example of that on this fork.

items.title: A BotW run is two workloads, and blending them invented a result
items.verdict: `drive-botw.sh` spends its first ~4,050 frames in menus at 113 draws and 33.27 ms, then ~4,750 frames of gameplay at 3,516 draws and 49.90 ms. A whole-file median lands wherever the phase ratio falls and **describes no frame that occurred**.
items.note: This is not hypothetical. It produced a confident **"−6.2% GPU busy"** for a change whose real effect is +0.5%, because two runs of the same script had slightly different menu-to-gameplay ratios. `telemetry-report.py` now segments by draw load and analyses the longest phase. Any BotW number in this repo predating it is suspect.

items.title: `cp_fence` is the vsync timer — solved, and never a defect
items.verdict: The fence releases **10 µs** after a vsync signal (p99 30 µs), exactly one vsync and one flip per stall, and the duration is identical in a 113-draw menu and in 3,516-draw gameplay. That is frame pacing working.
items.note: **Do not try to recover this 15.58 ms.** It retroactively explains why parking the spin and committing work early both changed nothing — the guest was never waiting for the GPU. One flip per vsync also pins `swapInterval = 1`, so the grid is 16.68 ms and a 49.90 ms frame is the title taking three slots.

items.title: The GPU's dead air: 33 ms idle per 50 ms frame, in two blocks
items.verdict: The idle is not diffuse — it is two large contiguous gaps, which is what made the next commit's single-cause explanation findable.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — cp_idle and the GPU's 33 ms of dead air

items.title: BotW is 20 fps instead of 30 because of one config default
items.verdict: `gpu.frame_critical_path_ns` is **35.25 ms** against a two-slot deadline of 33.27 ms, so the frame takes three slots. Turning off **`GX2DrawdoneSync`** drops it to 18.64 ms and the scene to **30.06 fps**, deterministic across n=3 / n=2.
items.note: The cost is `GX2DrawDone`'s `IT_HLE_SYNC_ASYNC_OPERATIONS` packet, which BotW emits twice per frame and whose handler force-finishes readbacks with bare `waitUntilCompleted()` on the Latte thread: **6.78 ms/frame, of which 6.75 ms is texture-readback force-finish**. **The default was not changed** — it is a documented accuracy tradeoff, and that is a product call.

items.title: The `MTLEvent` wrap was real, and fixing it corrects every `gpu.busy_ns` ever recorded
items.verdict: `EVENT_VALUE_WRAP` was 4096, so the signalled value went backwards every ~29 s and periodically disabled command-buffer serialisation. `gpu.busy_ns` sums per-buffer intervals, so overlapping buffers were **double-counted**.
items.note: **Do not compare `gpu.busy_ns` across this commit.** The same scene reads 16.8 ms properly serialised against 19.1–19.4 before. The inflation grows with run length — the first wrap is ~29 s in — so old figures are inconsistently wrong, not uniformly so. Frame time and critical path were unaffected. The same commit fixed an uninitialised read; both were confounds.

items.title: Give command buffers a timeline instead of a pointer identity
items.verdict: Identity by pointer is unsound when the allocator reuses addresses. A monotonic timeline makes the ordering questions answerable at all.

items.title: What BotW actually reads back: 21 KB of float arrays per frame
items.verdict: Small, GPU-computed float arrays the guest genuinely consumes — delivered by draining the pipeline. The readback is not spurious, which is why the drain cannot simply be removed.

items.title: Reconcile CLAUDE.md, the README and the porting plans with the code
items.verdict: **Fourteen stale or wrong claims corrected in one pass**, across five documents.
items.note: The direct motivation for this status page: fourteen hand-typed facts had drifted from the code at once, and nothing in the workflow would have caught them.

items.title: Pass-structure audit on the open world — the shrine verdict does not transfer
items.verdict: 202–203 render passes, **73–74 of them same-FBO splits (36%)**, 804 MB/frame of attachment traffic, and **390 depth-sampled draws** where the shrine had zero. **95.0–95.1% of the splits come from one call site**: `bufferCache_copyStreamoutToMainBuffer`.
items.note: The old TBDR verdict rested on "the GPU is idle" and explicitly invited revisit on a GPU-heavy title; Korok gameplay met that precondition. The earlier 1,749 MB/frame estimate was 2.2× high — the formats had never been confirmed.

items.title: The GPU is ALU- and texture-bound, so the streamout work is cancelled
items.verdict: The premise was verified before the code was written, and it was false. **ALU and texture are the top limiter in 86.1% of active samples; the memory path in 12.8%.** Removing 300 MB/frame would relieve a subsystem that bottlenecks the GPU about an eighth of the time.
items.note: Per the plan's own gate: report and stop rather than build it anyway. The *other* gate passed and is recorded for whoever revisits — `gpu.streamout_read_fragment` is **0** against a vertex control of 1,136/frame, so a vertex-only intrapass barrier would be legal. The first version of that detector read zero on both counters because the scope was self-defeating; the control is the only reason it was caught rather than published.
items.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The GPU is ALU- and texture-bound

items.title: Three surfaces that lied about accurate barriers on Metal
items.verdict: A config default, a Debug menu checkbox and a startup log line all reported a setting **nothing reads**. `CheckIfRenderPassNeedsFlush`, its declaration and its call site have been inside `/* */` since `26e40a4` — it arrived already-commented in the upstream Metal PR and has never run.
items.note: The fork therefore runs permanently in the barriers-off regime: the speed is already banked in every number here, and the correctness cost is already being paid. The setting itself was kept, inert, so `settings.xml` round-trips and the self-dependency work has something to hang off.

items.title: This page, and the rule that keeps it current
items.verdict: One generated page for what changed versus upstream, what was tried and what it measured. Commit list, diffstat, baseline rows and counter totals are read from the repo — only verdicts are hand-maintained. CI reports any commit that lands without a ledger entry.
items.note: It caught its own first bug: the counter parser read **114** against the real 113, matching the `TLM_COUNTER(...)` example inside the `.def`'s own header comment. Two self-references bound the design — a ledger entry cannot name the hash of the commit containing it, and the page embeds the commit that carries it — so CI advises rather than blocks, and `--check` is local-only.

refuted.title: The `MTLEvent` chain is what holds the frame back
refuted.verdict: `queue_latency_ns` (14.29 → 14.69 ms) and `command_buffers` (7 → 7) do not move between the 20 fps and 30 fps arms. Confirmed a second way by the wrap fix: buffers **had** been overlapping for most of every run, and it bought nothing.

refuted.title: The command-buffer commit threshold is mistuned
refuted.verdict: Same evidence as above — `command_buffers` is identical in both arms. Tuning when work is submitted cannot move a frame that is waiting on work already submitted.

refuted.title: The renderer is withholding work while the command processor blocks
refuted.verdict: True, and irrelevant. Work was held in **139,491 of 139,512** idle notifications per frame; committing at stall entry drops that **85%** and moves nothing else — frame time, fps, `cp_fence` and GPU busy all flat to within 0.6%.
refuted.note: The two notification sites look identical to the CP and are nothing alike: `RingStarvation` fires ~129,000×/frame inside a park-and-recheck loop, `FenceStall` once. Committing on the first would mint a command buffer per spin.

refuted.title: The readback drain can be made surgical
refuted.verdict: Measured three ways, all negative. `readback_forcestart` is 0, `readback_age_at_wait_ns` is 14.19 ms (the transfers had already been running ~7 ms each), and `readback_draws_ahead` is 169/frame against 3,516 draws — the blit is not stuck behind its own command buffer either.
refuted.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The readback drain is not surgically improvable

refuted.title: Exempting the readback command buffer from the event chain will help
refuted.verdict: n=3 per arm, **every performance range overlaps**: frame 49.90 both, critical path 35.13–35.22 vs 35.10–35.23, force-finish 6.21–6.34 vs 6.14–6.27. The only separated metric was `command_buffers` 7 → 9, which merely proves the arm was live.
refuted.note: Note the control-vs-control pair from that batch: `readback_forcefinish_ns` swings **±2% between identical runs** while frame time and critical path are stable to 0.0%. A "3% improvement" in that counter is noise.

refuted.title: An in-pass streamout copy will recover the 1.90 ms
refuted.verdict: Cancelled by its own gate before being built. It would have removed 300 MB/frame of redundant tile traffic from a GPU that is bandwidth-limited **12.8%** of the time.
refuted.note: Unblocked only if the ALU bottleneck is ever addressed and bandwidth becomes the limiter. The legality question is already answered in its favour.
refuted.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The GPU is ALU- and texture-bound

refuted.title: `IT_MEM_SEMAPHORE` or the wait-for-flip spin is costing time
Snapshotting guest threads at fence-stall entry will show what blocks
refuted.verdict: Found the cores idle 95% of the time — against their 96% baseline idle rate. **A probe with no control sample cannot discriminate.**

refuted.title: The ring-buffer `wfe` park is saving CPU
refuted.verdict: It is a no-op. `sched_yield` is **36% of a core** in the same path.
refuted.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The ring-buffer wfe park is a no-op

refuted.title: Charging a flat cycle cost per HLE call will fix the timing divergence
refuted.verdict: A hypothetical 500 cycles/call sums to **25,103,500 against 15,384,240 actually retired — 163%.** It would more than double emulated guest time. Any charge must be tiered per function.

traps.title: A BotW telemetry run is two workloads, and the split is ~50/50
traps.body: ~4,050 frames of menu at 113 draws and 33.27 ms, then ~4,750 of gameplay at 3,516 draws and 49.90 ms. `--skip=60` removes none of it. A whole-file median describes no frame that occurred, and because two runs never have the same ratio, **that difference reads as a treatment effect**. It manufactured a confident −6.2%. Always pass `--phase=<gameplay>`.

traps.title: MK8's attract mode is not a fixed workload
traps.body: It cycles demo scenes with very different draw loads, so two traces taken minutes apart are not comparable and neither are their sample counts. A first A/B read as "4.4× faster" from sample counts; the real figure was 1.77×. To compare implementations, put a runtime toggle behind an env var, flip it every ~20 s **inside one process**, discard windows that straddle a switch, and report the median of n≥5 per variant.

traps.title: `xcprof compare` reports share of CPU, not absolute CPU
traps.body: If total CPU drops, everything that survives looks like a regression — it reported 15 of them for a change that cut CPU nearly in half. Use it to see *which* frames left the profile; use absolute process `cputime` over a fixed wall-clock window for the magnitude. Prefer `ps -o cputime=` deltas over `%cpu`, which is a decaying average.

traps.title: Do not divide BotW's GPU time by 16.67 ms
traps.body: BotW targets **30 FPS**, so the budget is 33.3 ms. An earlier revision divided by the 60 FPS budget and concluded the GPU was at "108–147% of budget" and "is what caps the frame rate" — both wrong. At ~50% duty cycle it is not the limiter in this scene, and cutting GPU time 16% moved the frame rate not at all.

traps.title: `cemuLog_log` does not write to stdout
traps.body: It writes to `~/Library/Application Support/TesseraEmu/log.txt`. Grepping the process's redirected stdout for errors — or for your own instrumentation — silently finds nothing and reads as "clean". Use `--verbose`. And `CemuApp::OnExit` calls `_Exit()`, so **`kill -9` loses buffered log and shader-cache writes**.

traps.title: Scripted edits fail silently
traps.body: Source uses tabs; a heredoc written with spaces will no-op a Python `str.replace` and report success. Worse, an anchor that is not unique attaches your counter to the wrong call site — that happened, and put a counter on the *temporary* render-pass path, reading 2–4 passes/frame instead of 202. It was caught by arithmetic, not by review. Prefer explicit line ranges and always `git diff --stat` before building.

traps.title: An in-process scope timer cannot measure a fiber switch
traps.body: `Fiber::Switch` does not return until the fiber is resumed, so the timer measures descheduled time. It reported **197 ms of "busy" inside a 49.9 ms frame**. A microbenchmark is the right instrument.

traps.title: A pixel diff of the MK8 title screen proves nothing
traps.body: The "Press A to start" prompt pulses and the background animates, so **~22% of pixels differ between any two captures**. Use targeted instrumentation to show a rendering change is live. Relatedly, `capture-scene.sh` uses `screencapture -R`, which grabs a screen *region* — raise the window first or you capture whatever is on top of it.

roadmap.title: Shader cost — the ALU and texture work in the MSL the Latte decompiler emits
roadmap.verdict: Where the counters now point, and the only remaining frame-rate lever in this scene. Ordering- and bandwidth-shaped work is closed by measurement.
roadmap.gate: None — the measurement that closes every other avenue is what opens this one. But it is a materially different project from anything attempted so far and should be scoped rather than started from momentum.

roadmap.title: Item 3.1 — implement render-pass self-dependency on Metal
roadmap.verdict: A real correctness gap, not a latent option: anything sampling a render target while writing it currently reads undefined data. BotW lava and waterfalls are the known cases.
roadmap.gate: None. But expect it to **cost** frame rate — splitting passes for self-dependency raises pass count, the very thing the bandwidth work was trying to reduce. Shipping wrong pixels quietly is worse than shipping fewer frames honestly.

roadmap.title: `MTLBinaryArchive` — stop recompiling every shader on every launch
roadmap.verdict: The persistent cache stores pipeline **state descriptors**, not compiled binaries, and replays them on the loading screen. The `MTLBinaryArchive` code that would fix this exists in `MetalPipelineCompiler.cpp` and is entirely commented out.
roadmap.gate: None. Highest-value item in the graphics plan after the correctness backlog; affects launch time rather than steady-state frame rate.

roadmap.title: In-pass streamout copy (revive)
roadmap.verdict: Would remove ~70 same-FBO pass splits and 300 MB/frame. The legality question is already settled in its favour — `gpu.streamout_read_fragment` is 0, so a vertex-only intrapass barrier is legal on Apple silicon.
roadmap.gate: **The ALU bottleneck must be addressed first** and bandwidth must become the limiter. Today it relieves a subsystem that bottlenecks the GPU 12.8% of the time.
roadmap.ref: 00-master-plan.md — The GPU is ALU- and texture-bound

roadmap.title: Batch streamout copies to a pass boundary (fallback)
roadmap.verdict: Turns ~70 splits into ~1 per boundary without needing any intrapass barrier. Needs a dirty-pending-copy bit forcing a flush on first read.
roadmap.gate: Same gate as the in-pass copy, and moot while the GPU is ALU-bound.

roadmap.title: Hand-written AArch64 fiber switch
roadmap.verdict: Measured at 70× — 454.5 ns → 6.5 ns, worth 1.43 ms/frame at 3,143 switches. Real, and not a frame-rate fix.
roadmap.gate: Do it for power and headroom, not for fps: the work in a frame already fits one vsync period with 16.6% headroom, so removing 1.4 ms crosses no boundary.

roadmap.title: Tiered per-function HLE cycle charge
roadmap.verdict: An accuracy gap, not a speed one: guest threads issue a million library calls a second at zero emulated cost, including calls that on hardware are IPC round trips to IOSU.
roadmap.gate: A flat charge is **ruled out by measurement** — it would inflate guest time to 163%. The histogram shows the volume is cheap primitives and the expensive calls are rare, so the tiering must be per function.

roadmap.title: AArch64 backend peephole pass
roadmap.verdict: There is currently none — the only one that existed was x86-specific and was deleted with the backend. The `IMLUtil_*` helpers were kept as substrate for a replacement.
roadmap.gate: Profile before picking a codegen target. Both idle-wait bugs found in Stage 5 were invisible to the instruction-count metric the plan had ranked first.

roadmap.title: Offset-0 addressing-mode fold
roadmap.verdict: Named in the CPU plan as the highest instruction-count win available.
roadmap.gate: Same as above — the CPU is 18% busy in the scene that limits us, so this buys headroom, not frames.

roadmap.title: Cycle counting as a first-class IML register
roadmap.verdict: The largest single win in the CPU plan for loop-heavy code.
roadmap.gate: Wants the differential correctness harness (02, item 0.3) in place first.

roadmap.title: FMA — a correctness fix that also removes instructions
roadmap.verdict: Strictly more correct than the current lowering, and cheaper. The trap is the PPC↔ARM mnemonic crossover.
roadmap.gate: Gated on the differential correctness harness (02, item 0.3).

roadmap.title: Epoch-based JIT code reclamation
roadmap.verdict: Deliberately not built. The leak was instrumented instead, and reclamation waits on that counter showing a problem.
roadmap.gate: The leak counter has to demonstrate a problem worth this much machinery.

roadmap.title: Reconcile the two contradictory Shrine measurement sets
roadmap.verdict: Two instruments disagree: 28.6 fps / 149 passes / ~1190 draws / 15.6 ms GPU versus 30.06 fps / 132 passes / 3784 draws / 14.0 ms. Different counting (draw *calls* vs draw *sequences*), and the GPU figures predate the `839466d` `busy_ns` fix.
roadmap.gate: None — one run with the current harness settles it. Until then, quote neither.

roadmap.title: Notarization and stapling in CI
roadmap.verdict: Signing from CMake is done; notarization is not. Needed before the DMG is distributable to anyone who did not build it.
roadmap.gate: None technical — needs credentials in CI.

roadmap.title: Housekeeping: an unincremented counter and 19 stale locales
roadmap.verdict: `gpu.pipelines_compiled` is declared and never incremented. ~30 changed `_()` strings are untranslated across 19 locales.
roadmap.gate: None. Small, unglamorous, and neither blocks anything.
